messages:
Priya Nair: Heads-up: vendor released a switch-fabric microcode fix. We need a rolling soft-reboot of top-of-rack switches in az21. Proposed window: Tue 2025-09-02 02:00-06:00 UTC. Aiming for minimal disruption but expect brief task reschedules.
Alex Soto: Is this purely networking? Any planned GPU node reboots?
Priya Nair: Networking-only patch, but we cordon nodes connected to affected racks for controlled drains (~10-20m per rack) so pods reschedule elsewhere. Anticipate a transient GPU serving capacity dip ~10-15% at peak.
Jared Kim: Can we cohort to reduce blast radius? e.g., 2 racks per cohort with validation between cohorts?
Priya Nair: Yes. Plan: 4 cohorts (2 racks each). Steps: seed caches on standby nodes -> run canary on rack-az21-c1 -> if good, proceed cohort 1 (rack A+B) -> wait 30m -> cohort 2 -> etc. Canary scheduled at 02:00 UTC.
Marta Lopez: I'll draft outbound comms to Dedicated customers in az21. Also tag tickets for any high-SLA tenants.
Alex Soto: What's our abort criteria during canary?
Priya Nair: Abort if p95 latency > 150ms or error rate > 1.5x baseline for >3m, or if scheduled job failures appear in scheduler logs. Rollback plan: revert microcode and hot-reboot switches.
Jared Kim: How are we pre-warming KV and prefix caches? That usually causes a spike when nodes start serving.
Priya Nair: We'll run our cache-seed job from the ops jumpbox ahead of each cohort. Commands:
```
ssh jumpbox
./cache-seed --region=az21 --pools=standby --days=1 --parallel=8
kubectl label node rack-az21-c1 canary=true
```
Priya Nair: Also we have an automated routing policy to divert to eu-west1 for affected tenants if cohort health <90% for >3m.
Alex Soto: Backfill plan and cost impact?
Priya Nair: Use reserved warm pool first. If reserved nodes hit >80% used, we'll spin spot instances. Estimated incremental cost for the maintenance window: ~$900 expected, up to ~$1,500 worst-case with spot spinups and cross-region egress.
Marta Lopez: Draft comms text: "Scheduled network maintenance in az21 may cause brief request latency spikes and short task reschedules between 02:00-06:00 UTC on 2025-09-02. We'll stagger changes and monitor closely; rollback plan in place." Add canary + abort thresholds.
Jared Kim: I'll monitor scheduler and eviction logs. Please ping me when the canary cordon starts.
ops-bot: Maintenance calendar event created: az21-switch-microcode-roll 2025-09-02 02:00-06:00 UTC. Invite sent to #eng-infra, oncall, and infra-owner group.
Priya Nair: Ops checklist (short):
- create calendar event + add maintenance tag
- run cache-seed for standby nodes before canary
- label canary node and run validation harness (latency, errors, qps smoke tests)
- cohort drain: cordon -> kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -> verify telemetry -> uncordon on rollback
- enable short-circuit fallback routing to eu-west1 if cohort health <90% for >3m
- escalate to oncall if p95>150ms or errors>1.5x

Alex Soto: Add a note to block ML eval jobs during the window (they tend to be heavy). Also set a maintenance lock in the scheduler so no new long-running batches start.
Priya Nair: Good point. Added a blocked window 01:30-06:30 UTC for large eval batches. I'll put the exact rack sequence and runbook in the thread before EOD.
Marta Lopez: I'll send customer advisory and cc legal for tone.
Jared Kim: I'll be oncall for the window. Ping when canary starts and when each cohort begins.
Priya Nair: Will do. Keep rollback steps handy: microcode revert + switch warm reboot procedure documented. Thanks everyone.
